name: Isolated Left Bronchial Isomerism

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Radiologic and Anatomic Diagnostic Criteria for Bronchial Isomerism

criteria.description: Presence of bilateral left-sided bronchial morphology characterized by symmetrical hyparterial bronchi
No associated congenital heart defects or heterotaxy syndrome features
Confirmation of bronchial anatomy via chest CT or bronchoscopy showing left bronchial isomerism
Normal splenic anatomy without polysplenia or asplenia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria including bilateral left bronchial morphology, absence of cardiac malformations, and imaging confirmation must be met.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of heterotaxy syndromes with cardiac involvement.

pathognomonic.notes: Defining anatomical feature identified on imaging
searchTerms: both lungs with left bronchial pattern
left-sided bronchial structure on both sides

common.notes: Due to abnormal bronchial anatomy and impaired clearance
Persistent cough related to bronchial anomalies
Occasional breathing difficulty during physical activity
searchTerms: mild shortness of breath during activity

common.notes: No murmurs or abnormal heart sounds

occasional.notes: Localized airway dilation secondary to chronic infections
Reduced oxygen saturation during respiratory infections

rare.notes: Secondary to chronic lung disease in rare cases
Rare bleeding episodes from bronchial abnormalities

imaging: Chest CT demonstrating bilateral left bronchial morphology
Normal cardiac imaging without structural defects
genetic: No known specific genetic mutations identified
Genetic testing to exclude heterotaxy syndromes recommended
other: Normal splenic anatomy on abdominal ultrasound
Pulmonary function tests may show mild restrictive pattern

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of complex congenital heart defects
Associated with asplenia and severe cardiac malformations
Different bronchial branching pattern on imaging

redFlags: Recurrent severe respiratory infections requiring hospitalization
references: Brancati F, et al. Bronchial isomerism: clinical and radiologic features. Radiographics. 2019.
Orphanet: Isolated left bronchial isomerism. ORPHA:649029.
